scope.question: What did the Army independently require, select, validate, operate, retain, and leave unresolved across Anduril, Palantir, Raft, alternate implementation teams, commanders and Soldiers?

sources.title: Army emphasizes competition, invites feedback during NGC2 industry day
supports: Chief of Staff approval of a Capability Characteristics of Need in May 2024
joint planning by an Army Futures Command product owner and an acquisition program manager
an announced competitive and transparent acquisition strategy
a living requirements approach rather than a fixed monolithic specification
does_not_support: the complete Characteristics of Need bytes or change history
which vendor wrote any requirement
later source-selection results or operational acceptance
absence of concentration in a common component

sources.title: NGC2 becomes official program office at PEO C3N
supports: formal establishment of an Army NGC2 program office
a named government program manager and public acquisition chain
Army-wide mission and delivery responsibility
does_not_support: the full delegation and responsibility matrix
vendor acceptance or data-rights allocation
independent performance of any component

sources.title: Army announces NGC2 prototype award
supports: $99.6 million eleven-month prototype OTA to Team Anduril for 4th Infantry Division
requirement for an integrated and scalable hardware, software and application suite through a common integrated data layer
prototype rather than production status
Army statement that NGC2 is an ecosystem and a continuing competitive effort
does_not_support: full production acceptance
exclusive Anduril control
the complete team, evaluation or rights schedule
Palantir or Raft responsibilities in this award by itself

sources.title: Army announces additional competitive NGC2 award
supports: a separate $26 million prototype effort for another division
continued competition and different divisional implementation paths
an operated program-level counterfactual to a single closed Anduril implementation
does_not_support: equivalent technical depth or performance across the teams
competition inside every common component
successful replacement of the common data layer

sources.title: Ivy Division launches Army prototype for NGC2
supports: 4th Infantry Division use of an integrated operational architecture during Ivy Sting
continuing experimentation under increasingly contested conditions
Army, industry and Soldier application development
official statement that the tools do not replace the Soldier
does_not_support: a complete after-action report
independent verification of performance claims
the exact data and model versions
every override, abort, near miss or failure

sources.title: How the Army is putting the commander back in command and control
supports: Army-directed clean-sheet design and experimentation at Project Convergence
four-layer operational architecture
commander and Soldier tailoring of views and applications
claim that applications can be updated or discarded and technology will not replace commander judgment
reported identification of challenges and areas for improvement
does_not_support: a binding legal or technical veto for every user
complete rejection and override logs
independent acceptance testing
observed long-term absence of vendor lock-in

sources.title: Army leaders encourage industry to bring core strength to rapidly scale NGC2
supports: Army team-lead approach and competitive onboarding of vendors and components
best-of-breed and incumbent/non-incumbent teaming policy
continuing government invitation for integration into future divisions
does_not_support: equal bargaining or technical power among vendors
successful onboarding of every candidate
practical substitutability of the common data baseline

sources.title: Accelerating transformative technologies aids commanders' readiness across the Pacific
supports: 25th Infantry Division as a second operational implementation environment
full-stack experimentation and real-time Soldier identification of useful and deficient technologies
official statement that AI is a decision aid and commanders retain final judgment
does_not_support: the complete alternate-team responsibility matrix
a final production acceptance decision
every rejected component or operational defect

sources.title: Army and defense sector announce Right to Integrate sprint
supports: public-customer effort to require cross-platform integration and data sharing
a broad multi-vendor denominator beyond Palantir and Anduril
Army rather than one vendor as the announced integration sovereign
does_not_support: completed interoperability
equal interface rights
the NGC2 common data baseline decision by itself
common private governance

sources.title: Army and industry align on common data baseline as NGC2 moves from prototyping to delivery
supports: Army establishment of a common data layer baseline after operational validations and ten months of feedback
Anduril lead responsibility for the common data baseline
Palantir edge-to-cloud data mesh role through Foundry paired with Lattice
Raft responsibility for registries, transformation tools and data federation
Anduril as 4th Infantry Division full-stack implementation lead and Lockheed Martin as 25th Infantry Division full-stack implementation lead
movement from prototyping toward delivery while a later culminating division-scale validation remained planned
does_not_support: one-company ownership or governance
final production acceptance of every component
complete interface-control, data-rights, software-rights or transition terms
autonomous command or targeting
absence of later failure, replacement or redesign
